content: The clay says to the potter: You trample me today; but a day will come when I shall trample you under the earth.
author: Kabir
explanation: A stark, poetic reminder of human mortality and cosmic equality. All pride and material dominance will dissolve back into the earth from which our bodies were temporarily formed.
practicalInsight: Whenever vanity or arrogance arises regarding status or possessions, recall the clay's prophecy and re-ground in humility.
reflectionPrompt: How does the certainty of bodily dissolution change the importance of my current petty grievances?
